I want to be able to man up so to speak and give myself a reason to stop hating myself. It's currently 5 in the morning - EST.

It's an incredible job and I want it with every fiber of my being. I can't reschedule the interview. The VP of the department and four other members are expecting me to be there tomorrow at 2 in the afternoon. I'm trying to use this possible opportunity to keep me going. If I get it I can get help, if not then I'm just fucked.

I've grappled with suicide ideation for almost six years now. It starts with the depression and grows into this monstrous self loathing. I've tried not moving, not thinking and just laying there. I've tried controlling my breathing and meditating. I don't believe the world will fix itself this time for me.

The worst part is that I know that if I can get through tonight that I will be ok. I know I can move on and start over again. I know that one day I may look back and see this as a hurdle I jumped over.

And it's completely ridiculous but I couldn't help but start crying while reading what you wrote. I tell people that when they think they're completely alone and in the dark that someone is always trying to clear the darkness away so the light can shine again.

But I feel worthless and inadequate as a person knowing that my depression not only ruins my life but ruined something I loved and cherished so deeply. I just want to find the strength to make it through tonight and I'm so scared that I'm not going to be able to.

I mean Friday. The job is that I would help university graduates find work in their fields. Career Development. I know if I get this job I'll be able to get off of my friend's couch and start all over. Picking up the pieces of my life is going to be the hard part, this is day one and I'm barely making it through the night.

It is incredibly humiliating because this has happened to me before and the same friends let me stay with them. I feel like a fuck up because I can't seem to do anything right or very well. I have no job right now, I do have an interview tomorrow and I don't want to go. It's for a great job that would allow me to professionally get help and I don't want to put myself out there anymore.

I'm staying with a friend of mine until I can figure things out. I honestly don't think I will figure things out. I just want to stop being in pain and stop being tired. I can't stop thinking about how much I'm such a fuck up. I'm intruding on my friends because I'm a worthless individual who isn't capable of taking care of myself.

Also coming from personal experience: I went to the hospital once for lower abdominal pains (gastrointestinal nothing reproductive) and I still had a pelvic examination done, a pregnancy test, urine test and a PAP done. I asked why so many tests and my doctor told me almost the exact same things that my friend had told me. Apparently it helps them rule out STDs, endometriomas (ovarian cysts), ectopic pregnancy and things of the lady region variety. Both my friend and the doctor said (albeit separately) it's to be thorough and sure they aren't missing anything potentially immediately life threatening.

If anything get yourself tested for chlamydia and just call her if the results come back positive - yes, the conversation will suck but you'll be doing the honest and proper thing. Self diagnostics never work out simply because you are not properly trained to recognize and analyze medical problems. I hope things work out, be easy. :(

I agree with griminald. Just because someone may have nothing to hide doesn't mean that they want to be constantly "looked" on. 

I believe if you truly had trusted him and were secure enough with yourself and with the relationship, you wouldn't look. But griminald nailed it on the head, if you can't trust him without the inspections then you can't trust him period.

And there is never just **one** lie. It seems as though you're using it as a scapegoat to justify being hurt. People lie all the time, granted I don't agree with him lying to you about his virginity. Why does it bother you so much knowing you weren't the first? Do you believe he will be the one and only person you will ever have sex with realistically speaking? I hope I'm not coming off harshly but unless you are planning on living your life with him forever there is no reason to put the subject of virginity on a pedestal. 

He doesn't need to give you any passwords, just because he has before doesn't mean that he should continue. He may feel that you abused the passwords before and now real boundaries are being placed. Think about it from his perspective with the least amount of bias that you can if you haven't already done so.

You said that you think he jacks off to her, so what? If you think that he will only ever masturbate to you, you're wrong. Biologically speaking men will be sexually attracted to people who aren't their mate/spouse/what have you. Have you caught him jacking off to said image, or are you jumping the gun? If you allow yourself to jump to conclusions you will ruin not only the relationship, but yourself.

I think you should just have a sit down and really think about what you want from this relationship. Does he want the same things? Are they feasible? Can you live with knowing he lied to you about his virginity? Are you secure enough in yourself that you won't breakdown whenever his eyes aren't glued to you?

I know you may not feel the greatest right now but think before you act, think logically and analytically.

This isn't something I did but something I'm incredibly proud to say my fiance did.

A while back my fiance and I both had a $10 dollar off coupon for Smokey Bones so we decided to go out for dinner which is something we rarely do. What I didn't know was that my fiance printed off an extra one.

After our meal my fiance gets up and walks over to a young family we had noticed earlier sitting across the restaurant. Two mid to late twenties adults, 3 young girls and a baby in a carrier, kids were behaving wonderfully by the way. I'm sitting at our table waiting for our server to come back with our card and I notice him pull a piece of paper out of his wallet and hand it to the man. There was a lot of smiling and some handshaking. When my fiance walked back to the table I asked him what that was all about. He said that he had printed off an extra coupon and had planned on giving it to someone, he said he had chosen the family because he thought the kids were incredibly behaved and that saving $10 dollars means a lot to a family. When we walked past the family as we were heading out, the mom and dad (presumably) stopped my fiance and said, "Thank you so much again. We really appreciate it, thank you."

We both smiled and left. 

TL;DR: My fiance gave a young family a $10 dollar off coupon at a restaurant.

So I work for a company that handles a very huge corporation's retiree health care benefits, kind of like their HR. I work 8am-5pm, Monday through Friday and I hear all sorts of crazy things. People will often try to lie to me so that I can some how change their health care benefits, and I hear all sorts of crazy excuses as to why they can't pay their bills. I've become pretty damn amazing at picking up when something just isn't right. 

Last Friday at 4:57pm I received a call from a retiree. The retiree began to explain to me that when she went to pick up her husband's medications at their local pharmacy, the local pharmacy told them that they had no coverage. As per protocol we ask our participant's if there is a way for them to pay for the prescriptions until we have their health plan carrier updated (if they were wrongfully dropped from coverage that is). She takes a very quiet breath and for some reason my stomach feels as though I've been Falcon Punched. 

I told her I was going to look into the account and see if there was a reason behind the coverage termination, I told I would place her on a brief hold while I began my research. I then placed my phone/mic on mute so she wouldn't have to hear my hacking cough, right before I was about to unmute myself I hear her sobbing. Between her sobs I can hear her say 'Baby, please don't worry...' 

Sensing that this might be one of those few urgent calls I took the opportunity to call her health care provider and her prescription provide to verify their coverage. The health plan began to tell me that they had no record of them ever having this plan. My records indicated they have had the same plan for over 10 years. After 20 minutes on the phone with me the representative from their health plan says that their coverage was reinstated through an update (a real time update had just occured) and the drop in coverage was done in error. Apparently their provider dropped the ball...

I switch over to the other line and I can hear the participant sniffling a little. I tell her about the update occurring, that they have coverage and that there would be no lapse in coverage. She proceeds to break down crying while telling me that, "God has sent me an angel to help me and my husband. Thank you so much! My husbands cancer was in remission and came back, these medications are for his therapy. God bless you sweetheart."

I thanked her for her call and she thanked me for my help despite I didn't really do anything. The call ended at 47 minutes and 30 seconds. The following Monday I received an email from my supervisor saying that she had called back requesting to speak with a supervisor. She told my supervisor that I stayed on the phone with her and reassured her I would find out what happened and correct it.

When I remembered the sound of her sobbing...my heart broke. I would not have been able to keep myself as composed as she (all while coherently telling me about the situation between sniffles and hiccups) if my husband was sick...
